stateSheets.triangle:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a coherent static state-design contact sheet of ONLY the TRIANGLE character from the supplied approved eight-character cast. The source is an identity reference; output the selected character repeated in SIXTEEN different expression/activity poses, not the whole cast.
Character: soft inflated rounded triangular prism, upper tip and two lower corners, reference top-left. ONE MAIN COLOR: electric lemon yellow, throughout the body, arms and legs; lighter/darker values of this same hue only. Exactly TWO WHITE gloves with WHITE cuffs and TWO BLACK chunky rounded ankle boots with BLACK soles in every pose. Preserve the character's identity, facial style, silhouette, soft 3D volume and proportions. Material is opaque soft matte-satin silicone, with diffuse studio light, gentle rounded shading, no rainbow gradients. Dark eyebrows, white eye whites and black pupils; expressive sculpted mouth. No white cheek spots, no extra features, limbs or accessories.
Performance personality: Jaunty and enterprising. Snappy asymmetrical brows, small forward leans and brisk compact gestures; never angry or bossy.
Create EXACTLY 16 full-body poses arranged in an orderly FOUR COLUMN by FOUR ROW square grid. Every figure is the SAME character at identical visual scale. Show entire body, arms, gloves and boots within each cell with generous margins. Near-black background, soft neutral boot highlights for clear visibility. Changes must come from the face, eyes, brow, posture and gestures; no extra objects or abstract symbols. No bounding boxes. No title. Under each cell use one small crisp light-gray uppercase sans-serif label exactly as specified. Do not repeat the same smile and pose across all cells. Eye direction and hand gestures must differentiate cognition and task states clearly. No text on the character.
Read left to right, top to bottom:
1. HAPPY — Genuine cheerful eye-crinkle and big smile, arms relaxed slightly open, tiny pleased body lift. Distinct from the thumbs-up completion pose.
2. CURIOUS — One eyebrow raised, small body tilt, one white glove lightly at cheek, attentive small smile.
3. SURPRISED — Eyes noticeably wide, small round O mouth, both palms briefly held outward at chest level; surprise without fear.
4. CONFUSED — Uneven brows, uncertain crooked closed mouth, clear small tilted pose, one glove near the top side as if scratching head.
5. CONCERNED — Inner brows gently raised, soft direct eye contact, small sympathetic closed mouth, one open hand reaching slightly forward; not crying.
6. PLAYFUL — One clear wink, jaunty smile, slight sideways lean, one hand making a playful small wave.
7. IDLE — Relaxed neutral eyes and small closed smile, both hands resting by sides, feet planted; clear reference/rest pose.
8. LISTENING — Wide attentive forward gaze, mouth closed, slight forward lean, one cupped white glove beside the body as if listening.
9. THINKING — Eyes look up and to one side, a white glove under the mouth/chin, gently furrowed brows, other arm relaxed.
10. RESEARCHING — Eyes deliberately scan toward screen-right, upright alert pose, one white glove lightly above the eyes in a looking-out gesture, other hand low; no magnifying glass.
11. WORKING — Focused eyes directed slightly down, mouth closed, both gloves in front at waist height making small precise task gestures, steady stance.
12. ANSWERING — Friendly engaged forward gaze, open speaking mouth, one hand open in an explanatory presenting gesture, the other lower.
13. NEEDS INPUT — Patient questioning eye contact, one brow raised, both open palms clearly facing upward in a balanced shrug, mouth small and closed.
14. COMPLETE — Pleased smile, decisive clearly visible thumbs-up with one white glove, tiny celebratory heel lift, other hand relaxed.
15. ERROR — Brief concerned asymmetric brow and small uneasy mouth, one open palm turned outward in a gentle pause signal, both feet planted; recoverable problem, not rage or panic.
16. SLEEPING — Both eyelids fully closed, relaxed small smile, hands resting loosely, body inclined slightly to one side, both boots supported. No bed, no Z letters.
High-resolution square sheet, comfortably spaced, visually precise 3D character expression exploration. Keep all sixteen triangle bodies electric lemon yellow; white gloves and black boots in all sixteen. No props, no particles, no background scene, no clock hardware, no animation-strip frames or motion trails. These are static state concepts.

Eye direction and hand gestures must differentiate cognition and task states clearly. No text on the character.
Read left to right, top to bottom:
1. HAPPY — Genuine cheerful eye-crinkle and big smile, arms relaxed slightly open, tiny pleased body lift. Distinct from the thumbs-up completion pose.
2. CURIOUS — One eyebrow raised, small body tilt, one white glove lightly at cheek, attentive small smile.
3. SURPRISED — Eyes noticeably wide, small round O mouth, both palms briefly held outward at chest level; surprise without fear.
4. CONFUSED — Uneven brows, uncertain crooked closed mouth, clear small tilted pose, one glove near the top side as if scratching head.
5. CONCERNED — Inner brows gently raised, soft direct eye contact, small sympathetic closed mouth, one open hand reaching slightly forward; not crying.
6. PLAYFUL — One clear wink, jaunty smile, slight sideways lean, one hand making a playful small wave.
7. IDLE — Relaxed neutral eyes and small closed smile, both hands resting by sides, feet planted; clear reference/rest pose.
8. LISTENING — Wide attentive forward gaze, mouth closed, slight forward lean, one cupped white glove beside the body as if listening.
9. THINKING — Eyes look up and to one side, a white glove under the mouth/chin, gently furrowed brows, other arm relaxed.
10. RESEARCHING — Eyes deliberately scan toward screen-right, upright alert pose, one white glove lightly above the eyes in a looking-out gesture, other hand low; no magnifying glass.
11. WORKING — Focused eyes directed slightly down, mouth closed, both gloves in front at waist height making small precise task gestures, steady stance.
12. ANSWERING — Friendly engaged forward gaze, open speaking mouth, one hand open in an explanatory presenting gesture, the other lower.
13. NEEDS INPUT — Patient questioning eye contact, one brow raised, both open palms clearly facing upward in a balanced shrug, mouth small and closed.
14. COMPLETE — Pleased smile, decisive clearly visible thumbs-up with one white glove, tiny celebratory heel lift, other hand relaxed.
15. ERROR — Brief concerned asymmetric brow and small uneasy mouth, one open palm turned outward in a gentle pause signal, both feet planted; recoverable problem, not rage or panic.
16. SLEEPING — Both eyelids fully closed, relaxed small smile, hands resting loosely, body inclined slightly to one side, both boots supported. No bed, no Z letters.
